summary: Discovery call focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Main themes: SDK/agent support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture for routing, rate limits and quotas per route, observability hooks and logs for per-model routing, and security (KMS, SOC2, VPC). Customer is leaning toward a hybrid approach but needs performance benchmarks and clear guidance on rate-limit behaviors and caching to estimate costs.
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Voss (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (Nova Payments, Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng), Alyssa Park (Security)

Summary: quick intros, goals, current stack, integration questions re SDKs/agents and gateway/proxy, then security/Q&A and next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, Liam is our SE and Sara's on for any onboarding/CSM questions.
[00:10] Priya Singh: Hi thanks, Priya here; we run the fraud model infra at Nova, we are evaluating inference options for chat and embeddings - mostly around latencies for critical flows and cost for large volumes.
[00:25] Carlos Mendes: quick note, we have an internal gateway/proxy that sits in front of all external APIs; we need to understand how Redwood integrates behind that and whether we need special routing for dedicated nodes.
[00:40] Liam Ortiz: great, that's helpful. quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted API (simple REST/SDK), Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). From an integration perspective we support standard HTTP SDKs, official Python/Node clients, and there are example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[00:58] Priya: can you share specifics on the LangChain adapters? we have a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline that uses LlamaIndex in some services and LangChain elsewhere.
[01:10] Liam: yes - our SDK exports a LLM wrapper compatible with LangChain's LLM class, plus a vector embeddings client that LlamaIndex can call directly. we have sample notebooks; caveat: naming sometimes off in the auto docs, e.g., model_aliases get mapped to internal variants.
[01:28] Alyssa Park: on security, two questions: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping and can we run the control plane in our VPC?
[01:40] Maya: for Private deployments yes we support customer-managed KMS and a private control plane in VPC or on-prem. for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations too; hosted supports encryption at rest and you can integrate with your HSM via enterprise onboarding. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs after.
[01:58] Priya: about the gateway - we want to route low-latency traffic to dedicated pools and cheaper batches to hosted. how does routing work?
[02:15] Liam: you can route by policy: region, latency SLO, cost tier, or model variants. Redwood's routing layer can be fronted by your gateway - either call the Redwood API directly from the gateway or deploy a lightweight proxy that forwards traffic and injects routing headers. we also support token/prefix-based cache hints so dedicated nodes can use KV/prefix caching.
[02:39] Carlos: important: our gateway enforces rate limits per customer tenant; what are Redwood's rate limit semantics and how do quotas map?
[02:52] Liam: Hosted has per-key rate limits and billing quotas; for Dedicated you define throughput capacity (rps) and we expose per-route quotas and token quotas. we also provide per-token cost breakdowns in the Console. note that we recommend configuring a request token budget and using the SDK's client-side backoff/retry to handle spikes - we can show sample middleware for the proxy.
[03:18] Priya: does Redwood enforce hard throttles or soft throttles? we need predictable behavior for our critical flows.
[03:25] Liam: Dedicated environments can have hard SLO-based throttles at the pool level; hosted defaults to soft rate limiting with 429 responses under sustained bursts but we can negotiate stricter SLAs under a contract.
[03:40] Priya: good. on observability: we need tracing hooks and ability to drop logs into our ELK/Datadog. what are the observability integration points?
[03:52] Liam: Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level latency breakdowns, and exported traces. we have a tracing hook that emits spans compatible with OpenTelemetry and can forward logs to your logging endpoint; we can also enable higher fidelity request/response auditing for Private deployments.
[04:12] Carlos: for the PoC we'll need to measure p50/p95/p99 and token costs for our 2 main flows; can Redwood's bench script replay anonymized traces?
[04:22] Liam: yes - our SE team provides a bench harness that replays requests at configurable concurrency with prefix caching enabled/disabled. we can run both hosted and dedicated against the same traffic to compare.
[04:35] Priya: another question - how do LangChain agents handle streaming and function/tool calling with Redwood? we are using streaming for the UI chat.
[04:47] Liam: streaming is supported in our SDKs; LangChain integrations rely on the same streaming client under the hood. function calling is supported and we surface structured outputs; minor differences may exist in event ordering due to server vs client buffers - we note that in our LangChain examples.
[05:05] Alyssa: on compliance, we need audit logs, SSO (SAML/Okta), and RBAC. also data residency in EU for certain customers.
[05:16] Maya: we support SSO via SAML, RBAC roles in the Console, audit logs with configurable retention, and Private or Dedicated deployments can be hosted in EU regions. we'll include those details in the security packet.
[05:30] Carlos: can you explain caching - you mentioned prefix/KV cache - how does that interact with rate limits and billing?
[05:42] Liam: prefix/KV caching is a runtime optimization: repeated prefixes or KV cache hits return results without re-running the full model and that lowers token consumption. billing still accounts for cache-eligible vs cache-hit differently - cached hits are much cheaper. for hosted, caching is best-effort; for Dedicated you can tune cache sizes and eviction. caching reduces both latency and cost for high-repetition queries.
[06:05] Priya: what's the typical lift to integrate the SDK and the LangChain wrapper? we have two engs to dedicate for a PoC.
[06:14] Sara Voss: Onboarding for a basic PoC (SDK + LangChain examples + small bench) usually takes 2-3 days with our SE support; full production hardening (RBAC, KMS, private networking) takes longer. we provide runbooks and an integration repo.
[06:30] Carlos: any gotchas with model versioning and rollouts? we need to canary new model weights and fallback to older variants automatically.
[06:41] Liam: yes, Redwood has rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible variants. you can pin versions per-route. we also tie quality monitoring to eval sets so regressions trigger alerts.
[06:56] Priya: cost question: if we use dedicated for critical paths and hosted for long-tail, how do we estimate token cost transfer overhead when routing between them?
[07:07] Liam: routing itself is just a call; the cost is model compute where inference occurs. if you route small/latency critical calls to Dedicated those tokens incur dedicated rate; if longer async batches hit hosted you'll be billed hosted. there's some networking overhead but negligible compared to compute tokens; we provide cost modeling spreadsheets.
[07:28] Priya: competitors - we already trialed OpenAI and Anthropic; cost was a blocker for scale and embeddings quality varied.
[07:35] Maya: understood - we can run a side-by-side benchmark in the PoC.
[07:40] Carlos: any rate-limiter recommendations for the gateway? we want to avoid 429 storms.
[07:47] Liam: recommend token-bucket on the gateway with adaptive backoff and jitter; the SDK has client-side retry helpers. you can also set per-route soft limits and circuit-breakers in Redwood.
[07:59] Priya: ok great. final things - can you share a sample LangChain notebook and the bench harness?
[08:06] Maya: yes we'll drop links to the GitHub examples and the bench script.
[08:12] Alyssa: please also include the SOC2 report and KMS integration checklist.
[08:18] Maya: will do.
[08:22] Priya: timeline wise, we aim to pick a path by end of month; PoC next week would be awesome.
[08:29] Maya: recap: Redwood to send pricing + security docs + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, SE to schedule PoC bench and we'll run hosted vs dedicated tests with your sample traffic.
[08:40] Carlos: thanks all, talk soon.

End of call.
